transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You're not the first to come down after someone they love.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can't wait. My brother Omar is somewhere near this well.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Slow your breath before the dark leans closer. It hears hurry. Who did you lose?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My brother. Tell me what this place is doing to him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Questions cost here and fear pays double. Stand still and give me one at a time.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What is this well taking from people?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It steals you in pieces — names first, then faces. Stare too long and you'll forget who you came for.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You sound like you've been here too long.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Forty years by this fountain. I stopped fighting that truth. The place has been eating me slowly, but not enough to take what I know.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then you know how to last down here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I know how to last a little longer by this fountain. Nothing more. Survival is narrow and it charges interest every hour.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What hunts around us?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Some things kill fast. The watching ones are worse — they wait for a mistake and they have all the time the well keeps stealing from you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The shadows in the stone houses — what do they want?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: They answer to fear first, then sound. Light irritates them, so they remember you for it. Don't stare back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Do the jinn come out and take people?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: They don't rush. They wait until you hand yourself over without noticing. That is how most people are lost here — not grabbed, just slowly given.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What about the gate? The daughter they whisper about?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The king's daughter stands near it. She is not a fight, she is a test. She listens for what you want more than what you say. Answer wrong and the well learns you faster.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there anything that actually works against the dark here?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light the dark remembers how to fear. When it's called, the shadows pull back and the reaching hands hesitate. Saying even that much costs me, so listen carefully.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then give me the prayer that calls it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Not yet. I need to know if you want it to fight or to survive. Answer me straight, because the well is listening.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I want to survive long enough to keep Omar from fading.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That answer weighs less, and that matters here. The oil settles when you choose living over winning. Hold that shape.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't chase a fight with it. Just tell me how it works.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It isn't a blade you swing. It's a flare you spend — and it fades fast. Use it wrong and you stand empty while the dark stays. Call it only when the shadows close in, not before.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And the pale hands in the oil — does it stop them?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It pushes them back. It doesn't end them. They remember where you stood, and they wait. The prayer buys breath, not victory.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then what do you lose when you give it to me?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Time slips when I think about saying it — like a blink that lasts too long. Faces I should know go thin. The well keeps them. Giving this means I don't get those back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll carry that loss if it keeps Omar whole.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Fear is bleeding through you. I can hear it even when you don't. If you want me to finish this, hold him quieter inside — the oil perks up when brothers' names are near.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm trying. He's all I have.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My fingers won't steady, and that's the price showing itself. There was a pause just now where I couldn't find my own face. It frightened me more than the dark ever did.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Don't stop. I'm still here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The square tightens every time I lean toward this. The black surface learns what it hears and keeps it. I'm giving this because you chose surviving, not winning — and that choice costs me less.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm ready. Don't let the well finish your sentence.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. Don't spend it here — the well tightens when it's spoken twice. Keep it for when the shadows stop waiting and start moving.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: There's more. I can feel you holding something back.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is. And it costs more than the first. My hands won't stop and the oil is rising toward the rim. When I say it, you say nothing — not a breath, not a word.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't make a sound.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I'll hold them until I need them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Remember this too: the light is real but brief. It is not a weapon. It is a reminder to the dark of what it used to fear. Use it as that and it will last.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't forget what you paid for this.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: When you carry them out, carry one more thing. Hanash, from your valley, the one who never made it home. Say it where the sun can hear it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll bring your name back to the surface. I swear it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then go. The well has been patient with us, and patience here always runs out the same way.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not coming back without him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I know. I could see that from the moment you landed.
